explanation: Cultural Atlas notes it is considered impolite in Egypt to point the toe, heel, or sole of the foot toward another person, or to show the sole of your shoe, since the foot is viewed as the lowest and least clean part of the body. This applies in homes and any seated social setting, not just formal occasions.
local_tip: Keep your feet flat on the floor or tucked beneath you, and avoid resting an ankle on a knee in a way that points your sole at anyone.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and most impure part of the body, making it a serious insult to point them at someone.
Pointing the soles of your feet at someone is disrespectful, especially in traditional or formal settings.
Generally seen as casual, though it can seem out of place in a formal setting.

sources.title: What behaviours are rude in the Middle East
